correctness.rationale: The original graph-ball maximal inequality reduces without relaxation to every sign assignment and every selected positive averaging radius. There are exactly 53,860 finite rational LP branches for n=6,7,8,9. The standalone standard-library checker reconstructs each primal matrix and verifies a nonnegative rational dual with 1,039,232 exact integer inequalities, bounding the objective by (n−1)/n. Point-mass witnesses attain each limit. Finite verification suffices here because the analytic reduction is exhaustive over all real inputs; it is not a numerical extrapolation.

originality.rationale: Direct inspection of the most relevant recent full-text finite-graph classification through five vertices and earlier primary graph-maximal articles gives no theorem implying the four exact C6-C9 upper bounds. A general point-mass lower bound alone does not establish a sharp upper bound. Search-index and inaccessible older specialized papers are residual priority risks, so this is qualified best-knowledge originality, not a uniqueness certificate.
residual_risks: An equivalent inequality for these finite cycle sizes may have appeared in unindexed earlier work or under periodic/discrete BV terminology.

value.rationale: The natural open sharp-variation problem on cycles beyond previously classified graphs of up to five vertices is settled for two complete new diameter layers: C6 and C7 (diameter 3) and C8 and C9 (diameter 4). The four results supply exact attained constants and exhaustive all-input certificates when multiple graph-ball radii compete, rather than isolated computational data. The scope is a meaningful finite cutoff; no claim is made for all n.
